# dsh-personal-agent
> **Research prototype for reference only, not an official DeepSeek product.** This code grew out of
our team's day-to-day development work, with much of the engineering done by coding agents. Treat i
t as research code, not production-ready software. It may still contain bugs, and its coding style a
nd engineering practices may be inconsistent. Review and adapt it before using it in your own enviro

nment.
>
> We have adapted it for publication, so it is not identical to our internal version or the
implementation described in *Exploring Super-agent Design: Towards a More Autonomous Agent System*.
Some designs discussed in the article are directions for future development and are not implemented
ssed in the article are directions for future development and are not implemented in this prototype.
This fork keeps the prototype's architecture and turns it into a personal agent for one person, publ

ished as
`dsh-personal-agent`: https://github.com/yinguobing/dsh-personal-agent. In Chinese it is **

搭档** — the person you work
alongside, who keeps the notes and runs the errands, and asks before deci
ding anything. The package name is the only renamed identifier: plugin ids, the `orchestrator` servi

ce and the
`orchestrator_*` tools still carry the prototype's names, so `git diff` against upstream
hestrator_*` tools still carry the prototype's names, so `git diff` against upstream stays readable.
dsh-superagent is a proactive coding agent for one GitHub repository, packaged as a bundle for DeepS
eek Harness. It listens to GitHub and, optionally, Feishu. When someone allowed asks the agent for w
ork, it opens a work item, works on it in its own agent session and directory, and answers in the or
iginal conversation, for example with a pull request. A web panel shows what needs a person.
It is also a way of working with an agent: **take as little human attention as possible, and give as
much value as possible.** An agent that can act for a whole team can also waste a whole team's atte
ntion, so it acts only when asked or when a rule the team wrote allows it, and speaks only when some
one must act or can use a result. docs/000-philosophy.md explains the principle and what it asks of
or can use a result. docs/000-philosophy.md explains the principle and what it asks of the operator.
## Install it as a personal agent
This fork turns the prototype into a personal agent for one person: talk to it in the panel or on We

Chat, drop material
into a folder it watches, and it opens a work item only when you ask or a rule a

p material
into a folder it watches, and it opens a work item only when you ask or a rule allows it.
From a clone, one command installs it into its own DSH profile and writes the settings it needs:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
From the release tarball, install the package and write that configuration yourself; `examples/profi

le.cordis.patch.yml`
is the configuration the script would have written:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Installing straight from git is not supported: the build output is not committed, and pnpm asks for

a per-commit
approval before it runs the build.
It creates the profile from the shipped web template, installs this bundle and the memory index, wri

tes the settings
the agent needs (including worker permissions that never wait for an approval), and

prints the command that starts it
and where its material folder is. Pass `--no-memory` to install w
ithout long-term memory. It cannot supply a model key: without `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` in `<home>/.creden

tials.yaml` every turn
fails, and the installer says so.
The panel opens on a simple surface for the person — a conversation, the things in flight, and what

the agent would
like to do — while the operator's tabs sit behind one toggle. Then read docs/using.m

d for the first five minutes, docs/memory.md for how it
remembers things, and docs/known-gaps.md for
what is not yet solid. If something does not work, the gaps list is the honest inventory of where t
yet solid. If something does not work, the gaps list is the honest inventory of where to look first.
## Setup
The rest of this file describes the prototype this fork started from. Its setup has many steps, so a

n agent does it
with you. Ask your coding agent:
> Read SETUP.md in this repository and set up dsh-superagent with me.
It asks one short question at a time, shows the full plan once, and then installs and configures eve
rything. SETUP.md is what it follows.
## Documentation
Read the numbered documents in order; each builds only on the ones before it.
